extracted.intended_audience: research organizations, principal investigators, and applicants preparing proposals in response to ONR BAA N00014-22-S-B002
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a complete technical and budgetary proposal (Grants.gov R&R forms and attachments) responding to ONR BAA N00014-22-S-B002, following required sections, certifications, and administrative rules. Includes technical narrative, management, budget, data management, compliance, and required forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Compliance (Fields 4a-4d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields 4a through 4d - Environmental Compliance: Address these fields and briefly indicate whether the intended research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory, and how the applicant will ensure compliance with environmental statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies and recipients must comply with environmental planning/regulatory requirements (e.g., NEPA). Refer questions about NEPA or other environmental planning or regulatory compliance issues to the technical point of contact. Most ONR field research falls under NEPA categorical exclusions; lab research complying with other safety/environmental/resource laws is typically excluded from further NEPA documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA consideration for Federal actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) requires agencies consider the environmental impact of 'major Federal actions' prior to any final agency decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award constitutes a 'major Federal action' (40 CFR 1508.18), NEPA documentation such as an EIS may be required even if only providing grant funds. Most ONR-funded field research is covered by categorical exclusions, but applicants should consult the technical point of contact for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract (Field 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field 7 – Project Summary/Abstract: Leave Field 7 blank; complete Form SF424, Project Abstract. If an error message occurs when leaving Block 7 blank, upload the Project Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not type project summary in Block 7; rely on SF424 Project Abstract field. If Grants.gov forces an entry, upload a Project Abstract file instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (Field 8) and attachment format
rubrics_metrics.description: Field 8 – Project Narrative: Describe clearly the research, including the objective and approach to be performed, keeping in mind the evaluation criteria. Attach the entire proposal narrative to R&R Other Project Information form in Field 8 as a single PDF file. (Save the file as 'Technical Proposal,' as typing in the box is prohibited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach technical proposal as one PDF under R&R Other Project Information. The narrative must describe required sections (cover page, TOC, technical approach, management, PI qualifications, etc.) as specified in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover Page: This must include the words 'Technical Proposal' and the following: (a) BAA Number; (b) Title of Proposal; (c) Identity of prime Offeror and complete list of sub awards, if applicable; (d) Technical contact (name, address, phone/fax, electronic mail address) Administrative/business contact (name, address, phone/fax, electronic mail address); (e) and; (f) Proposed period of performance (identify both the base period and any options, if included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all contact information and award-identifying information are present; label the document 'Technical Proposal'. Clearly identify prime and subaward relationships and periods of performance (base + options).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of Contents: An alphabetical/numerical listing of the sections within the proposal, including corresponding page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear TOC referencing all sections and page numbers to facilitate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Approach (research plan and innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Approach. Describe the scientific or technical concepts that will be investigated, providing the complete research plan. Describe what is innovative about the proposed approach. Describe the proposed approach compared to alternate approaches other researchers in this field have taken. Given a successful completion, describe the results, new knowledge, or insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a complete, coherent research plan including hypotheses/goals, methods, novelty, comparison to alternatives, and anticipated outcomes. Link methods to objectives and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future Department of Defense Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Future Department of Defense Relevance: A description of potential relevance and contributions of the effort to the agency’s specific mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the work maps to DoD/ONR mission areas and how expected results will be useful to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Schedule and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Schedule and Milestones: A summary of the schedule of events and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a timeline and measurable milestones; tie milestones to deliverables and evaluation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports (required progress and final reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports: The following are sample reports that are typically required under a research effort: Technical and Financial Progress Reports; Final Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for periodic technical and financial reporting and a final report. Note ‘Grants do not include the delivery of software, prototypes, and other hardware deliverables.’

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Management Approach. Describe the overall management approach and provide rationale for participation of key team members. Describe the planned relationships with any subawardees or collaborators. This is a single PI award; if there are subawardees or collaborators, explain how the proposed team fits the single PI structure. If appropriate, briefly describe anticipated schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain organizational roles, responsibilities, communication, and how subawards/collaborations will be managed under a single-PI structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator Qualifications: A discussion of the qualifications of the proposed Principal Investigator and any other key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide CV/biosketch and narrative demonstrating PI and key personnel experience, expertise, and fit to perform the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Responsibility information
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility: Offerors must provide the following information to ONR in order to assist in ONR's evaluation of the offeror's responsibility: Describe how you have adequate resources or the ability to obtain such resources; Describe how you have the ability to comply with the grant conditions; Describe your performance history; Describe your record of integrity and business ethics; Describe qualifications and eligibility to receive an award under applicable laws and regulations; Describe your organization, experience, accounting, and operational controls and technical skills, or the ability to obtain them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply evidence of management capability, financial/technical resources, past performance, integrity, eligibility, and internal controls (property control, QA, safety programs). ONR may request additional details before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (<=2 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Management Plan: In no more than 2 pages, discuss the following: The types of data, software, and other materials to be produced; How the data will be acquired; Time and location of data acquisition, if scientifically pertinent; How the data will be processed; The file formats and the naming conventions that will be used; A description of the quality assurance and quality control measures during collection, analysis, and processing; A description of dataset origin when existing data resources are used; A description of the standards to be used for data and metadata format and content; Appropriate timeframe for preservation; The plan may consider the balance between the relative value of data preservation and other factors such as the associated cost and administrative burden. The plan will provide a justification for such decisions; A statement that the data cannot be made available to the public when there are national security or controlled unclassified information concerns (e.g., 'This data cannot be cleared for public release in accordance with the requirements in DoD Directive 5230.09.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise DMP addressing each listed item, justify any decision not to share or to limit preservation, and cite DoD Instruction 3200.12 where relevant. Include formats, naming conventions, QA/QC, and preservation timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References (Field 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field 9 – Bibliography & Referenced Cited: Upload your Bibliography/Referenced cited as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete references as one PDF attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources (Field 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field 10 – Facilities & Other Resources: Describe facilities available for performing the proposed research and any additional facilities the applicant proposes to acquire at its own expense. Indicate government-owned facilities already possessed that will be used. (Additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by any other practical means.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional, laboratory, and other resources available and any planned acquisitions funded by the applicant; explain why government-furnished equipment is not required if requesting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment (Field 11) and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Field 11 – Equipment: Describe any equipment available or any additional equipment the application proposes to acquire at its own expense. Indicate government owned equipment that will be use. Justify the need for each equipment item. (Additional equipment will not be provided unless the research cannot be completed by any other practical means.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize proposed equipment and justify necessity. General purpose equipment (PCs, office equipment) should not be requested unless used primarily/exclusively for the project; for computers include statement how integrated into program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Grants.gov R&R Budget forms and option period costing
rubrics_metrics.description: The offeror must use the Grants.gov forms (including the Standard Form (SF) Research and Related (R&R) Budget Form) from the application package template associated with the BAA on the Grants.gov web site. If options are proposed, the cost proposal must provide the pricing information for the option periods; failure to include the proposed costs for the option periods will result in the options not being included in the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the R&R budget form(s) provided with the solicitation and include explicit costs for all option periods you propose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification attachment (Section K)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate Adobe .pdf document should be included in the application that provides appropriate justification and/or supporting documentation for each element of cost proposed. This document shall be attached under Section K. 'Budget Justification' of the Research and Related Budget form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a thorough, itemized budget justification as PDF under Section K using 'Add Attachment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Labor cost detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Labor – Individual labor categories or persons, with associated labor hours and unburdened direct labor rates. Provide escalation rates for out years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each labor category/person, hours, unburdened rates, and escalation assumptions; round all costs to nearest dollar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and Clerical Labor charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and Clerical Labor – Salaries of administrative and clerical staff are normally indirect costs (and included in an indirect cost rate). Direct charging of these costs may be appropriate when a major project requires an extensive amount of administrative or clerical support significantly greater than normal and routine levels of support. Budgets proposing direct charging of administrative or clerical salaries must be supported with a budget justification which adequately describes the major project and the administrative and/or clerical work to be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only directly charge admin/clerical labor when exceptional; include strong justification describing the extraordinary workload and tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits and Indirect Costs (rates and calculations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe Benefits and Indirect Costs (Facilities and Administration (F&A), Overhead, G&A, etc.) – The proposal should show the rates and calculation of the costs for each rate category. If the non-Federal entity has never received a negotiated indirect cost rate, they may elect to charge a de minimis rate of 10% of modified total direct costs or provide sufficient detail to enable a determination of allowability, allocability and reasonableness of the allocation bases, and how the rates are calculated. See 2 CFR 200.414(f) regarding the use of a de minimis rate. Additional information may be requested, if needed. If composite rates are used, provide the calculations used in deriving the composite rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit indirect rate tables, calculation methods, and support documentation. If using de minimis, state election and ensure compliance with 2 CFR 200.414(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost detail and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel – The proposed travel cost must include the following for each trip: the purpose of the trip, origin and destination if known, approximate duration, the number of travelers, and the estimated cost per trip must be justified based on the organizations historical average cost per trip or other reasonable basis for estimation. Such estimates and the resultant costs claimed must conform to the applicable Federal cost principles. Offerors may include travel costs for the Principal Investigator to attend the peer reviews described in Section II of this BAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize trips with purpose, destinations, durations, travelers, and per-trip cost basis. Ensure conformity with federal cost principles and include PI peer-review travel if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards/Subcontracts documentation and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Subawards/Subcontracts – Provide a description of the work to be performed by the subrecipient/subcontractor. For each subaward, a detailed cost proposal is required to be submitted by the subrecipient(s) using the R&R budget form. A proposal and any supporting documentation must be received and reviewed before the Government can complete its cost analysis of the proposal and enter negotiations. ONR's preferred method of receiving subcontract information is for this information to be included with the Prime's proposal. However, a subcontractor's cost proposal can be provided in a sealed envelope with the recipient's cost proposal or via e-mail directly to the Program Officer at the same time the prime proposal is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full subrecipient cost proposals (R&R forms) with prime submission where possible; if separate, follow allowed methods and ensure timely receipt so government can conduct cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant cost documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants – Provide a breakdown of the consultant’s hours, the hourly rate proposed, any other proposed consultant costs, a copy of the signed Consulting Agreement or other documentation supporting the proposed consultant rate/cost, and a copy of the consultant’s proposed statement of work if it is not already separately identified in the prime contractor’s proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide signed agreements or supporting documentation for proposed consultant rates and a clear SOW and hours justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials & Supplies itemization
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials & Supplies – Provide an itemized list of all proposed materials and supplies including quantities, unit prices, and the basis for the estimate (e.g., quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize all consumables and supplies with unit costs and support for estimates (quotes or past costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Acquired Equipment or Facilities justification and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient Acquired Equipment or Facilities – Equipment and/or facilities are normally furnished by the Recipient. If acquisition of equipment and/or facilities is proposed, a justification for the purchase of the items must be provided. Provide an itemized list of all equipment and/or facilities costs and the basis for the estimate (e.g., quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists). Allowable items normally are limited to research equipment not already available for the project. General purpose equipment (i.e., equipment not used exclusively for research, scientific or other technical activities, such as personal computers, laptops, office equipment) should not be requested unless they will be used primarily or exclusively for the project. For computer/laptop purchases and other general purpose equipment, if proposed, include a statement indicating how each item of equipment will be integrated into the program or used as an integral part of the research effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify equipment purchases with necessity and integration into the research; avoid requesting general purpose equipment unless strongly justified and show how it will be primarily used for project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs itemization
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Direct Costs – Provide an itemized list of all other proposed other direct costs such as Graduate Assistant tuition, laboratory fees, report and publication costs, and the basis for the estimate (e.g., quotes, prior purchases, catalog price lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and justify miscellaneous direct costs with basis for estimates and support documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/event funding constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: NOTE: If the grant proposal requests funds for hosting or attending a conference, workshop or symposium: ONR will not sponsor an ONR, or DoD event. Provide a list of other sponsors and the requested amounts to be funded by all sponsors. The funds provided by ONR may be used to pay for food or beverages as a direct cost only in exceptional circumstances. The funds shall not be used for food or beverages unless (a) The grant proposal contains a request for such funding that is fully supported factually in accordance with the cost principles of the relevant OMB Circular, and (b) The Grants Officer determines that the funding is a reasonable, allocable, allowable expense under the relevant cost principles. Specify in your proposal how the event and related outcomes will directly and programmatically relate to the Science & Technology Plan and identify specific focus areas that will be addressed. The proposal must provide the technical and scientific objectives of the program or event and clearly state the desired outcomes (e.g. conference proceedings, journal articles, algorithms, tools, additional research, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting conference funding, list co-sponsors and amounts, justify exceptional direct costs (food/beverage), and demonstrate direct programmatic relation to the S&T Plan and measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee/Profit prohibition under assistance agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee/Profit – Fee/profit is unallowable under assistance agreements at either the prime or subaward level, but may be permitted on contracts issued by the prime awardee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include fee/profit line items in grant/cooperative agreement/TIA budgets; contracts issued by the prime may include profit as permitted by contracting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) form will be used to collect the following information for all senior/key personnel... • Degree Type and Degree Year fields as the source for career information. • Current and Pending Support shall include a list of all current projects the individual is working on, in addition to any future support the individual has applied to receive, regardless of the source. The following information shall be included for each current or pending project: Title and objectives; The percentage per year to be devoted to the other projects; The total amount of support the individual is receiving in connection to each of the other research projects or will receive if the other proposals are awarded; Name and address of the agencies and/or other parties supporting the other research projects; Period of performance for the other research projects. • Upload the biosketch/CV/resume to the Biographical Sketch field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the expanded profile fully for PI and all senior/key personnel. Missing required information may cause ONR to deem the application incomplete and return it without further review. Upload biosketches as attachments where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Related Personal Data (demographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: This form will be used by ONR as the source of demographic information, such as gender, race, ethnicity, and disability information for the Project Director/Principal Investigator and all other persons identified as Co-Project Director(s)/Co-Principal Investigator(s). Each application must include this form with the name fields of the Project Director/Principal Investigator and any Co-Project Director(s)/Co-Principal Investigator(s) completed; however, provision of the demographic information in the form is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete name fields; demographic questions are voluntary and may be marked 'Do not wish to provide.' Demographic information may be accessible to reviewers but will not be considered in the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission: Grants.gov registration and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants shall submit their applications online through Grants.gov. Organizations must have an active System for Award Management (SAM) registration, and Grants.gov account. Create a Grants.gov Account, add a Profile, and have EBiz POC authorize appropriate roles (including AOR). The EBiz POC must authorize personnel who can make legally binding commitments. The name of the organization applicant with the AOR role that submitted the application is inserted into the signature line of the application, serving as the electronic signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin SAM and Grants.gov registrations well before the deadline (SAM may take time). Ensure EBiz POC assigns AOR role to an authorized person. The AOR submitting the application provides the legal electronic signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must NOT be submitted through the Grants.gov application process. White paper submissions must be submitted through FedConnect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow submission channel instructions precisely—use FedConnect for white papers and Grants.gov for full application packages as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments to grant applications submitted through Grants.Gov must be in Adobe Portable Document Format. Proposals with attachments submitted in word processing, spreadsheet, or any format other than Adobe Portable Document Format will not be considered for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert all attachments to PDF; name attachments (e.g., 'Technical Proposal') and ensure they open correctly before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace usage and submission timing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov applicants can apply online using Workspace. Creating a workspace allows you to complete an application online and route it through your organization for review before submitting. Grants.gov recommends submitting your application package at least 48 hours prior to the close date to provide you with time to correct any potential technical issues that may disrupt the application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Workspace to collaborate, complete mandatory fields (marked with asterisk), fill SF-424 fields first to pre-populate others, and submit early (>=48 hours) to allow time for technical troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of timely submission and receipt policies
rubrics_metrics.description: An electronic date/time stamp is generated within the system when the application is successfully received by Grants.gov. The applicant with the AOR role who submitted the application will receive an acknowledgement of receipt and a tracking number (GRANTXXXXXXXX)... Proof of timely submission shall be the official date and time that Grants.gov receives your application. Applications received by Grants.gov after the established due date for the program will be considered late and will not be considered for funding by ONR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain Grants.gov acknowledgement and tracking number as proof. Monitor inbox for Grants.gov and ONR retrieval acknowledgements; late submissions are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Qualifications (32 CFR 22.415 standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be qualified, a potential recipient must: (1) Have the management capability and adequate financial and technical resources...; (2) Have a satisfactory record of executing such programs or activities (if a prior recipient of an award); (3) Have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics; and (4) Be otherwise qualified and eligible to receive a grant or cooperative agreement under applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation and narrative demonstrating management capability, financial/technical resources, past performance, integrity, and legal eligibility to assist the Grants Officer in qualification determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS and integrity/performance review for larger awards
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total Federal share will be greater than the simplified acquisition threshold on any Federal award under a notice of funding opportunity: (1) The Federal awarding agency ... will review and consider any information about the applicant that is in the designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM (currently FAPIIS) (see 41 U.S.C. 2313); (2) An applicant, at their option, may review information in the designated integrity and performance systems ... and comment on any information about itself; (3) The Federal awarding agency will consider any comments by the applicant ... in making a judgment about the applicant’s integrity, business ethics, and record of performance ... when completing the review of risk posed by applicants as described in 2 CFR 200.206.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For awards above the relevant threshold, expect agency review of FAPIIS entries; applicants may view/comment on entries and should proactively address adverse items in submissions or attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) / 2 CFR Part 170 reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any company, non-profit agency or university that applies for financial assistance as either a prime or sub-recipient under this BAA must provide information in its proposal that describes the necessary processes and systems in place to comply with the reporting requirements identified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A. Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe processes/systems for subaward and executive compensation reporting; consult 2 CFR Part 170 and Appendix A for details and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certifications and required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Assistance Certifications Report is an attestation that the entity will abide by the requirements of the various laws and regulations... you are still required to submit any documentation, including the SF LLL Disclosure of Lobby Activities (if applicable), and disclosure of any unpaid delinquent tax liability or a felony conviction under any Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all applicable certifications and submit required supporting documents (e.g., SF-LLL) as part of the electronic proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Restrictions on Lobbying (> $100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants, cooperative agreement awards, and TIA awards greater than $100,000 require a certification of compliance with a national policy mandate concerning lobbying. Grant applicants shall provide this certification by electronic submission of SF424 (R&R) as a part of the electronic proposal submitted via Grants.gov (complete Block 17). The certification includes statements that no Federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid to influence officers or Members of Congress; if other funds have been paid, complete SF-LLL; require subcontract language at all tiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposals > $100k, complete Block 17 certifying lobbying status, and include required disclosures and flow-down language to subrecipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification re internal confidentiality agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submission of its proposal or application, the applicant represents that it does not require any of its employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements or statements prohibiting or otherwise restricting those employees, contractors, subrecipients from lawfully reporting that waste, fraud, or abuse to a designated investigative or law enforcement representative of a Federal department or agency authorized to receive such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 'I Agree' on SF424 Block 17 to certify non-use of restrictive confidentiality agreements that block lawful reporting of fraud/waste/abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding disclosure of funding sources (Section 223(a) of NDAA FY2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on the SF 424 (R&R) block 17 you agree ... that: (a) the PI and other key personnel certify that the current and pending support provided on the proposal is current, accurate and complete; (b) agree to update such disclosure at the request of the agency prior to the award of support and at any subsequent time the agency determines appropriate during the term of the award; and (c) the PI and other key personnel have been made aware of the requirements under Section 223(a)(1) of this Act. False statements may subject to penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PI and key personnel current/pending support disclosures are accurate and include agreement to update as requested; be aware of penalties for false statements (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest disclosure and compliance (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for assistance are required to comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c), Codes of Conduct, to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in the award and administration of any contracts by which a recipient or subrecipient purchases property or services, supported by federal funds. You and your organization must disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict of interest(s) to us. You must also disclose any potential or actual conflict(s) of interest for any identified sub recipient you include in your application. At our discretion, we may ask you for a conflict of interest mitigation plan after you submit your application. Your plan is subject to our approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all potential/actual conflicts for applicant and subrecipients; be prepared to propose and implement an ONR-approved mitigation plan if requested.
